newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan state airline begins capital restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Jordan state airline begins capital restructuring.

text.p: Jordan plans to go ahead soon with a debt-capital swap of its state carrier, the first step to a financial restructuring of the debt-ridden company for eventual privatisation, officials said on Sunday.

"The board of RJ (Royal Jordanian) has sent an official letter. We will definitely and officially in the near future approve this request...and we have to do it," Transport Minister Nasser al-Lawzi told Reuters.
Lawzi said the debt-capital swap, tripling the airlines capital to 210 million dinars ($297 million), was essential to bring the $650 million debt-ridden airline back on a sound financial footing.
It was also essential to proceed with a three-phased programme of restructuring, commercialisation and privatisation.
Lawzi said Saudi billionare investor Prince Walid bin Talal, with a wide portfolio in tourism and communications business, is studying investing seed money in the commercialisation stage of RJ.
This entails transforming it into a publicly listed firm with its shares initially owned by the government before divesting them to the public and foreign investors .
Lawzi said that Prince Walid's investment "would be a good vote of confidence in RJ's potential investment prospects scheme..it will attract a lot of other investors."
Prince Walid stressed RJ's key assets were its technical manpower and network of 48 destinations, officials said.

The capital restructuring includes transforming 110-120 million dinars ($169 million) owed to Jordan Petroleum Refinery Company, the state pension fund and commercial banks into RJ's new capital, Lawzi said.
The government will still have to work out the shape of the debt-capital swap, Lawzi added.

"If you talk about investors and privatisation, we have figures that are not internationally accepted and risky. When we do this capitalisation, this debt/equity ratio will be a better figure," Lawzi added.
"We have to start to really make preparations for other steps...and the first step is the capitalisation, the first prerequisite for restructuring, we cannot start without it."
"We will capitalise the debt of the refinery as part of the new RJ capital," Lawzi said.
Bulk of the RJ's debts were mainly incurred by aircraft purchases and leases of its 17 plane fleet composed of three Airbus 320, six Airbus 310, five Tristars and three Boeing 707.
RJ is going ahead with plans to re-lease its five Tristars to generate $40 million in cash, by an "international tender already announced for the lease of the planes," Lawzi said.
Lawzi said the government was evaluating a number of offers from international firms but has not made a decision yet.
The move will help ease debt servicing of over $50 million annually that eats away the airlines operational profits.

RJ officials say that they are studying a $200 million bond issue in global capital markets, as another part of the financial restructuring to refinance some of its loans and aircraft purchases. ($=0.708 dinar)
